title: བསྟན་འགྱུར། སྡེ་དགེ། ཚད་མ། ཡེ (Derge Tengyur, vol. 193)
shelf_note: Pramāṇa commentary on jāti (utkarṣa-, apakarṣa-, varṇya-, avarṇya-sama), the content of the Tshad ma section of the Derge Tengyur.

ocr_errors.problem: 'སྒྲ' (sound) appears dropped in the avarṇyasama example; sense recoverable from context

tr_errors_A.problem: 'arising immediately after effort' compressed; standard rendering

tr_errors_A.english: It likely follows Dignāga or Dharmakīrti’s systems
tr_errors_A.problem: speculative attribution in the meta note, not on the page

tr_errors_B.english: subtracts an intrinsic attribute from the subject to be proved
tr_errors_B.problem: Tibetan says 'another property'; 'intrinsic' is an added characterisation

tr_errors_B.english: the clay pot is already established and not something to be proved
tr_errors_B.problem: 'already established' interpolated into the quoted rejoinder (a correct gloss, but not in the text)

tr_errors_B.english: adds an extraneous attribute of the example

pages.prefer_reason: Neither has a serious error; A renders the apakarṣa and avarṇya definitions literally while B adds 'intrinsic' and 'already established' that are not in the Tibetan, so A is marginally more faithful.

adjudication.claim: 'intrinsic attribute' added where Tibetan has ཆོས་གཞན 'another property'
adjudication.why: Image line 6 reads བསྒྲུབ་བྱ་ལ་ཆོས་གཞན་འགྲིབ་པར་བྱེད་པའི་ཕྱིར; nothing corresponds to 'intrinsic'. Moderate, not serious.
Image line 7 has only བུམ་པ་བསྒྲགས་བྱ་མ་ཡིན་པ; addition is a gloss, minor.
B carries small additions absent from the Tibetan; A is closer, though the difference is small.

adjudication.claim: Check for any dropped or reversed passage in either version
adjudication.why: Both cover every sentence of the folio (ཕྱོགས་ཙམ explanation, the sogs lists, the 'only these' reply, four sama definitions) without reversal.

book_verdict: Correct leaf (printed 612), near-clean transcription, and two sound translations of a jāti passage; A is slightly more literal than B.
